scope: Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Chapters 17-18 (with Online Appendix A1.7, A1.8 and A1.13.1): Keynesian models with sticky prices. The static IS-Phillips model with adaptive versus rational expectations, the RE solution family and its infinite-past form (17.8); policy rules in both models with the stability and determinacy sets corrected (E7: phi > 1 or phi < -1 - 2/(sigma kappa)); AR(1) responses, super-Fisherian and open-mouth cases and the root eta*; any persistence with any sign and a long-run response of one ((17.14) inverse corrected, E8); the adaptive Taylor rule; the full model with its two-sided solution, the anticipated rate rise from minus infinity (Figure 17.5) and Figure 17.6 surplus changes (labels shown inconsistent); fiscal underpinnings (17.19) with the dating correction and Figure 17.7 numbers certified (E10); optimal policy with the x* = 0 intercept corrected (E9); Taylor determinacy with phi_x ((1.58); phi > 1 neither necessary nor sufficient only once phi_x < 0 is allowed; complex roots, E11; (1.55) entry corrected); Chapter 18 rules; links showing the simple model is exactly the beta = 0 case of the full model. Printed errors corrected with Lean counterexamples.
source: John H. Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Princeton University Press, Chapter 17, pp. 397-421, Chapter 18, pp. 422-432, and Online Appendix A1.7, A1.8 and A1.13.1, pp. 569-572 and 586-588.
